args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and review why it was promoted to production when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for it, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. A status check afterwards shows all three regions on v2.3.0, passing health checks, with an error rate of about 0.2%. This didn't need change-manager approval, since that's only required for versions that have never been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It lists two follow-ups: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before it's deployed again, and look into why it went to production when its staging release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
